title: Enhancement of hydrogen spillover onto carbon nanotubes with defect feature
material_description: as-prepared (before wash) | as-prepared CNT without Co impregnation and before HNO3 wash: MWCNT made by catalytic decomposition of C2H2/H2 (30/70) over Co0.05Mg0.95O catalyst at 973 K (Section 2.2), HCl-purified; tube diameters 5-15 nm; residual Co catalyst 1.02 wt.% (Table 1)
purification_method: 37% HCl to dissolve impurities such as the metal catalyst, filtered, washed in de-ionized water, dried at 373 K in air (purity >90%)
source_location: main-07.png (journal p. 555), Section 3.3 text, left column ('the weight change of the as-prepared CNTs was only 0.22 +/- 0.07 wt.%'); same value in Section 3.4 text, main-08.png (p. 556), left column ('the CNT without Co impregnation'); plotted as the 'before wash' as-prepared point of Fig. 9 (main-07.png)
notes: Printed 0.22 +/- 0.07 wt.%. Label taken from Fig. 9 (first figure showing the sample; x-axis category 'as-prepared', series 'before wash'). Residual Co from Table 1 (the paper implies Table 1 is before the HNO3 wash). BET 453 m2/g from Section 3.2 text. H2 uptake = weight change over a heating/cooling cycle in a TG (303 K -> 673 K at 5 K/min = desorption curve, then cooled to 303 K = adsorption curve) under 1 atm H2; not an equilibrium isotherm value. temperature_k 303 K = end of the adsorption (cooling) curve; reference_temperature_k 673 K = upper cycle temperature (desorbed state). Pressure printed '1 atm' / 'one atmosphere' (H2 flow at ambient pressure), stored as 1.01325 bar. uptake_type unspecified: the paper names no basis; basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default for a gravimetric value with a stated buoyancy correction ('the buoyancy effect was taken into consideration during heating/cooling. All weight changes ... were corrected using a quartz blank calibration [7]'). Degas fields = in-situ pretreatment step (1): heated to 673 K at 10 K/min, held 1 h in flowing H2 (20 ml/min), cooled to room temperature until constant weight (also the Co reduction step); this is in H2, not vacuum, and the paper does not call it degassing; printed 673 K -> 399.85 C. Sample mass printed 'Ten milligrams'. BET area by N2 at 77 K (Quantachrome Autosorb-1); no BET P/P0 range or consistency criteria stated; no numerical pore volume or average pore diameter printed (BJH PSD only in Fig. 6). Paper states 'All hydrogen storage experiments were repeated at least once.'
